newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Lebed calls attack on Chechnya deal insignificant.
newsitem.headline: Lebed calls attack on Chechnya deal insignificant.

text.p: Russian Security Chief Alexander Lebed on Tuesday dismissed as insignificant criticisms by Russia's interior minister of his peace deal in Chechnya.
"I am not in the habit of given attention to such insignificant things," Lebed tolds reporters in Brussels when asked about attacks on him.
"The dog barks and the caravan passes," he said.
Russian Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov on Monday renewed his assault on Lebed's peace deal saying the ceasefire was undermining Russia's ability to restore order in the breakaway republic.

Under Lebed's deal Russian troops, which failed to establish control over Chechnya in 21 months of bloody fighting, started withdrawing from the region last month. A decision on whether Chechnya would become independent was deferred for five years.
Lebed was in Brussels on his first visit to the West. He saw NATO leaders on Monday and was to visit SHAPE, the Strategic Headquarters Allied Powers Europe, in Mons, Belgium, later on Tuesday.
